question: ______ is the first of the 24 Tirthankaras of Jainism.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rishabhanatha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rishabhanatha, also known as Adinatha, is the first Tirthankara of Jainism.
 
• He is believed to have lived millions of years ago, with his time period not fixed but often considered to be in the pre-Vedic times.
 
• Rishabhanatha is said to have attained Kevala Jnana (omniscience) under a banyan tree.
 
• He is associated with the symbol of a bull and is often depicted in a meditative pose in Jain art and iconography.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tirthankaras:** In Jainism, Tirthankaras are spiritual teachers who have attained enlightenment and help others achieve liberation. There are 24 Tirthankaras, with Rishabhanatha being the first and Mahavira being the last.
 
• **Jainism:** An ancient Indian religion that emphasizes non-violence, truth, and asceticism. It seeks liberation through self-discipline and non-attachment.
 
• **Kevala Jnana:** This term refers to the highest form of knowledge or omniscience in Jain philosophy, achieved by Tirthankaras and other liberated souls.
 
• **Symbolism:** Each Tirthankara is associated with a specific symbol; Rishabhanatha's symbol is the bull, representing strength and endurance.
 
• **Rishabhanatha's Legacy:** He is often credited with teaching humans various skills, including agriculture, arts, and social organization, laying the foundation for a civilized society.
